subject: Recap + next steps: prompt samples, model candidates & PII redaction
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@nimbusdocs.com>, Jared Liao <jared.l@nimbusdocs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: prompt samples, model candidates & PII redaction

Thanks again for a productive discovery today — appreciate the clarity on the two main apps you want to ship (Doc summarization pipeline, and a conversational assistant for internal KB). Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can scope an eval and redaction plan.

Summary of needs
- High concision summarization for long legal/contract docs (target latency ~250ms for short requests, higher for long sequences)
- KB assistant that must not hallucinate and must enforce data retention controls and redaction for PII
- Volume: ~5M tokens/month to start, bursty during crawls

Preliminary model candidates (for evaluation)
- Redwood-Adapt-13B (quantized 8-bit) — low-latency baseline for assistant flows
- Llama-3-70B-Chat (8k) with KV caching — candidate for high-quality summarization when latency budget allows
- Mix: smaller adapt model for routing + larger model for expensive summarization jobs

What we need from you (action items)
1) Prompt sample set: representative queries across the two apps, including edge cases (PHI/PII examples, obfuscated inputs, partial docs). Use the attached prompt_intake_template.csv to structure.
2) Sensitive label guidance: for each sample, flag whether it contains PII/PHI/PCI/confidential IP. If you can, mask 1–2 items manually so we can test our redaction heuristics.
3) A small corpus (50–200 examples) for an initial redaction pass — we can run our automated check and return a redaction report within 48 hours once provided.

Links + artifacts
- Prompt intake template attached: prompt_intake_template.csv
- Benchmark folder (public): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nimbus-eval

Next steps (timeline)
- You: upload sample pack and label guidance by Fri 3/4
- Redwood: run redaction audit + baseline runs on two model candidates within 48–72 hours of receiving samples
- Joint: 30-min sync next week to review redaction report and pick the model for a 2-week eval

Attachments: [Attachment: prompt_intake_template.csv (CSV, 3KB)]

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter

Thanks Ben — great recap and the template is exactly what we need. A couple quick notes from our side: we can assemble the 50–200 sample pack but need clarity on two points before we send anything that might include customer PII:

- Do you need raw PII in samples or is masked/anonymized examples acceptable? We prefer to avoid sending raw emails/SSNs.
- Is there a preferred format for marking sensitive spans vs. whole-doc flags? We can add inline tags but would rather follow your intake template if it supports spans.

I'm attaching a small starter file so you can validate your redaction check on our format — it contains obfuscated names and one redacted credit-card placeholder.

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: prompt samples, model candidates & PII redaction

CC'ing Monica for the redaction checklist and implementation notes. Quick technical addendum from the eval team:

Model fit guidance (short):
- For short interactive KB queries: recommend Redwood-Adapt-13B (fast, cost-effective). We can enable conservative decoding + retrieval-augmented generation to reduce hallucination.
- For long-form summarization: run an LLM with extended context + prefix caching; Llama-3-70B-Chat gave best QA/summary fidelity in our internal bench for contract-like texts. We'll provide per-case token-cost projections once we run your sample pack.

Redaction checklist (what we'll run automatically)
1) Named-entity detection (PHI/PII/credit-card patterns) + heuristics for obfuscated items
2) Phrase-level masking preview: we return both a masked sample and an explanation of heuristics
3) Edge-case flags: e.g., partially redacted passport numbers, contract clauses with third-party PII
4) False-positive report so you can review and allow-list recurring tokens

Deliverables & timing
- We can accept your sample pack today or tomorrow. Once received, Redwood will:
  a) Run redaction audit and return a redaction_checklist.pdf plus a sanitized subset (within 48 hours)
  b) Run two baseline model runs (Adapt-13B and Llama-3-70B-Chat) against the sample set and upload perf + quality metrics to the shared drive (within 72 hours)
  c) Propose an eval candidate and estimated cost per 1M tokens after the first run

Small request for the sample pack format (so our automated tooling ingests it correctly):
- CSV columns: id | raw_text | masked_text | labels(comma-separated) | source_type (doc|kb|email) | priority
- If you cannot provide masked_text, leave blank but set labels consistently

Attachments: [Attachment: redaction_checklist.pdf (PDF, 7KB)]

If helpful, Monica can run a short demo of the redaction UI — Monica, can you take point on scheduling for next week?

Thanks,
Marissa
